what: Public Storage owns self-storage facilities. It is the largest operator in the United States, renting small lockable units to people and small businesses on month-to-month contracts, and it owns a stake in the European operator Shurgard.
customers: Households moving, downsizing or short of space, and small businesses storing stock and equipment.
money: monthly rent on units across roughly 3,000 US facilities
tenant insurance, merchandise and management fees
moat: Locations in dense urban areas where new storage is hard to permit, and a brand customers search for by name, which keeps marketing costs low.
risks: Demand depends on people moving house, which high mortgage rates have slowed
New supply in some markets has held down rents
Debt of about $12 billion is modest for a landlord but still rate-sensitive
Customers can leave with a month's notice, so pricing power cuts both ways
opportunities: Operating margin near 40% is very high because facilities need few staff
Existing customers accept regular rent increases once they have moved in
A recovery in house moves would lift occupancy and new-customer rates
watch: Same-store occupancy and the rate charged to new customers, which leads revenue.
